This doc's purpose is to provide speed optimal and slice optimal solutions for all 967 non-parity PBLs on Square-1.
This sheet uses Karnaukh notation, a notation designed to optimize algorithms for mass learning, consumption,
communication and internalization. If you have any recommendations for how to improve the document, please 
leave a comment, and any support is greatly appreciated :)

Inspired by/based off of PBL documents/resources 
made by: Stepan Makarenko, Michael Young,
Samuel Fang, Gil Zussman, and Dylan Baumbach

Foundation of document during early 
versions (e.g. Raw algs, alg tools): 
Daniel Goodman, Eva Kato

Charlie Harrison, Adrien Auvray Matyn, Samuel Fang,

PLL names are from Raul Low Beattie's PDF:
Corner headlights/bar on right, left, front or back
T perm, F perm, U perm
This is when the case is symmetrical along the X/Z axis.
This means double bars/double corner swaps on left and right, etc.
This is when the case is symmetrical along two diagonal axes.
You can hover your mouse over the cell and read the notes/alternate algs
This means put a separated corner at front right or front left.
This is when the case is symmetrical along one diagonal axis.
This means put the separated corner at front right, front left, etc.
Congrats! You can do this case from any angle.
A few notes about parity PBLs and how some of them conflict with the above definitions:

Because W perm has solved corners and no bars of any sort,
 the way I classify it for angling is by its two "opposite" edges. 
This is basically the "H perm" side of the W perm.

S perm doesn't have any bars or headlights at all. What I do is
 I consider the "J perm" side of the S perm to be the "bar".
Just treat the adjacent swap of edges as your "separated corner."
